items.m: French President Emmanuel Macron set an end-of-year deadline for an agreement on the European Union's next seven-year budget after the continent's leaders ruled out any chances for a deal to be reached at their summit on Thursday.

items.t: Live: Trump calls on Putin to end all 'military aggression' against Europe
items.m: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had urged his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". Although Trump did not provide any further details, he added that he hoped this would pave the way for a peace deal to be struck between Kyiv and Moscow. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

items.t: Trump unilaterally changes joint statement with NATO chief, adding warning for Ukraine not to escalate war, Politico reports
items.m: US President Donald Trump unilaterally edited the text of a joint statement with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Politico reported.

items.t: Four Jehovah's Witnesses convicted of 'extremism' in Russian-annexed Crimea
items.m: Nov 27 - Four Jehovah's Witnesses have been convicted of \"extremist\" activity in Russian-annexed Crimea and sentenced to up to eight years in prison, the faith group said, among the longest terms handed to members since Moscow banned the movement in 2017.

items.t: Russia’s hybrid war on Europe evolving, but failing: IISS
items.m: Growing attacks have damaged European infrastructure, but have not reduced support for Ukraine, analysis says.

items.t: Tyson Fury’s wife backtracks on claim boxer suffers from schizophrenia
items.m: Paris Fury had claimed mental health diagnosis for Tyson following his 2015 victory over Ukraine's Wladimir Klitschko.

items.t: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter
items.m: As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.

items.t: EU: Leaders fail to reach agreement on next budget after tense summit
items.m: At the bloc headquarters in Brussels on Thursday, EU leaders failed to reach a consensus after more than 12 hours of talks over the budget and a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year. France 24's Dave Keating tells us more.

items.t: ‘He’s an aggressor and a killer. He can’t be a friend’: Zelensky likens Trump calling Putin his friend to calling Hitler a friend during World War II
items.m: Volodymyr Zelensky said he finds it “strange” that Donald Trump has twice called Vladimir Putin his friend.

items.t: Crimean Court Jails 4 Jehovah’s Witnesses for ‘Extremism’
items.m: The jail terms are some of the longest handed down to members of the religious movement since it was outlawed by Russia in 2017.

items.t: North Korea halts Russia military aid over Seoul row, Kyiv says
items.m: Ukraine's military intelligence said Kim Jong-un personally ordered the suspension after Russia's deputy foreign minister said it would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.

items.t: Lukashenko claims he knew nothing about Russia’s invasion of Ukraine — then pulls out a map to show where it began
items.m: Alexander Lukashenko said in an interview with the French outlet Le Point that he did not know about Russia’s plans to invade Ukraine in 2022.

items.t: A Ukrainian journalist lost three family members during Russia’s offensive in Donbas. Her mother blames Ukraine. She set out to find the truth.
items.m: Anastasiya Gribanova is a journalist with BBC Ukraine. Her father, grandmother, and grandfather died in Donbas in early 2025 during the Russian army’s offensive. Anastasiya’s mother, who has supported Russia since 2014, blames Ukraine for their deaths. The journalist cut off contact with her mother and later tried to find out for herself who was responsible for her relatives’ deaths. She described the results of her investigation and how it affected her family’s relationships in a documentary and an article for the BBC. Meduza recounts her report.

items.t: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Over 40 Elderly Civilians in Belarus
items.m: The International Committee of the Red Cross said the exchange was part of ongoing humanitarian efforts to help reunite people from the two warring countries with their relatives.

items.t: Trump defends Putin friendship that Zelensky calls ‘strange’
items.m: Asked about their relationship, President Donald Trump said: “We want to make a deal,” blaming the Russian and Ukrainian leaders' “hate” as the biggest problem keeping them from peace.

items.t: Putin can't be a friend, he's like Hitler - Zelensky
items.m: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky said US President Donald Trump calling Russia's Vladimir Putin "my friend" was strange and akin to making the same comment about Adolf Hitler during World War Two.

items.t: Investigator says Russia is "brainwashing" Ukrainian children at so-called summer camps
items.m: Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, many Ukrainian children have ended up at Russian camps where the Ukrainian language is banned and the Russian anthem is played each day. More Sunday on 60 Minutes.

items.t: John Simpson: Ukraine is bowed but still unbroken as freezing weather sets in
items.m: Ukraine settles in for another devastating winter as the questions persists: how will it all end?

items.t: ‘Mass-casualty event’ in Europe possible amid rise in Russian sabotage, says thinktank
items.m: Report warns attacks on critical infrastructure could lead to demand for retaliation and expose EU divisions Russian sabotage attacks on Europe are increasing and a “mass-casualty event” is now possible as increasingly skilled operatives target critical infrastructure with ever more complex methods, a leading strategic thinktank has said. The International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) said in a report that Russian intelligence services and their proxies were targeting European railways, energy networks and defence industries in an attempt to weaken support for Ukraine. Continue readi

items.t: By Putin's logic, Russia should be returned to Mongolia, Belarus' Lukashenka says
items.m: The Belarusian leader said medieval history cannot justify territorial claims, since Russian lands were themselves once under Mongol rule, and traced East Slavic statehood to Kyivan Rus'. He then appeared to soften the remarks, saying Putin "perfectly understands this" and is "misinterpreted".

items.t: Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine's energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, causing deaths
items.m: After a series of Russian strikes and with the onset of winter cold, Ukraine was forced to halt all electricity exports, while imports reached their highest level since mid-June.

items.t: ‘No reports, no strikes’: Russia’s pro-war bloggers slam proposed prison sentences for sharing photos and videos of Ukrainian attacks
items.m: Yesterday, a group of Russian senators introduced a bill in the State Duma that calls for prison terms of up to five years for illegally distributing information about the aftermath of Ukrainian strikes, as well as terrorist attacks and sabotage. Bans on publishing photos and videos of attack aftermath are already in effect in many regions, though until now the punishment has only involved administrative fines. items.t: Russia has lost at least 87 members of its most secretive special forces unit since invading Ukraine, investigation finds
items.m: At least 87 members of Russia’s Special Operations Forces (SSO) have died since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, iStories, an independent Russian investigative outlet, found after examining a leaked Rosstat database of death records.

items.t: Ukrainian intelligence says North Korea has stopped sending troops and missiles to Russia
items.m: Military cooperation between Russia and North Korea has been suspended, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry intelligence directorate (HUR) said. The rupture followed a statement by Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrei Rudenko, who said Moscow would work to ease tensions between South Korea and North Korea in the future, according to the HUR.

items.t: Russia Extends Jet Fuel Export Ban Until March 2027
items.m: Moscow first banned jet fuel exports in June after Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries led to slumps in domestic production and shortages.

items.t: Zelenskyy: Trump calling Putin a friend like calling Hitler a friend
items.m: Volodymyr Zelenskyy described President Trump calling Vladimir Putin "my friend" as "strange" because the Russian leader is "an aggressor and a killer."

items.t: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview shows the peril of treating Putin like a corporate rival
items.m: Trump’s son-in-law and top negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars. items.t: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
items.m: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.

items.t: Ukraine: How much have Europeans spent on aid?
items.m: Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, EU member states have provided around €200 billion in aid to Ukraine, making them its largest contributors ahead of the United States. Germany leads in total financial contributions, with around €54 billion, roughly twice France's €27 billion. But the picture changes when aid is measured against GDP or per capita, with Denmark and other Nordic countries ranking among the biggest contributors.

items.t: Russia Accuses Latvia of Obstructing Grain Transit, Aiding Ukrainian Drone Attacks
items.m: Russia's Foreign Ministry accused Latvia on Friday of creating artificial obstacles to hinder the transit of Russian grain to global markets, saying the restrictions posed additional risks to global food security.

items.t: Italy challenges Zelenskyy's claims of coordination on Libya strikes
items.m: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani disputed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's account of coordination over attacks in Libya on Friday, accusing him of not telling the...

items.t: ‘Bear trap’: Ukraine hails new operation as Russian casualties mount
items.m: Russian assaults met with stout defence along the front as Western powers discuss ceasefire proposals.

items.t: Zelenskyy criticizes Trump for cozying up to Putin as EU kicks Ukraine funding down the road
items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized Donald Trump for cozying up to Putin, delaying delivery of promised Patriot missiles and not paying enough attention to the Ukraine war in an interview with the BBC that took place in Kyiv a day after the collapse of an EU budget deal that was to approve a $70 billion loan to the war-ravaged country.

items.t: Russian military flotilla bound for Libya turns around after warship sunk on Nov 22, sources says
items.m: PARIS/LONDON, Nov 27 - A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya has turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank a Russian naval corvette in Benghazi port on November 22, three people from military and security services told Reuters on Friday.
